The patient is an ___ year old woman w PMH HTN, HLD, OA, 
presenting with back and leg pain after a fall 2 weeks ago, 
course complicated by poor PO intake, found to have 
hyponatremia.

# Back and leg pain s/p fall: The patient has a history of 
recent fall while walking in the snow.

Fall appears to be a 
mechanical fall due to slipping in the snow.

No prodromal 
lightheadnedness, no LOC.

Xray shows compression fracture of L1 
of inderterminite age, per ortho consult it is likely an old 
fracutre and not acute.

R hip film shows no fracture over site 
of pian.

The patient's pain was controlled with standing tylenol 
and tramadol for breakthrough.
NSAIDs were DCed.

- Continues to complain of bilateral thigh pain -- on 
simvastatin.

Would consider checking CK if patient continues to 
have thigh pain beyond reasonable time frame and consider d/cing 
simvastatin
# Hyponatremia: The patient was found to have hypoNa to 117 at

On admission, FeNa 0.17, and the 
patient appeared dry on exam, suggesting hypovolemic 
hyponatremia.

Also, the patient has had low solute intake had 
has been drinking mostly water and tea, urine osms only 
moderately concentrated suggesting that the patient is taking 
too much PO free water.
Na improved to 130s at DC with IVF.

Diet 
was liberalized to avoid Na restriction.

- recommend rechecking BMP at next office to monitor for 
continued resolution of hyponatremia
# Bone health: The patient has a h/o OA.
L/S spine film shows
DJD and osteopenia as well as L1 compression Fx and kyphosis
L1/T12 of indeterminae age.
Vit D low.

Ca and Vit D were 
resumed.

# Social situation: The patient was living in the shelter long 
term because her home was condemned due to hoarding behavior.

The shelter has her on "medical ban" at this time since she was 
requiring too much care.

The patient denies current physical danger 
or abuse.
